2. Plaintiff respondents instituted O.C. Suit No.68 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif at North Raozan against the defendant appellants for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land. Plaintiffs' case was that Ahmed Ali was the original owner, grand father of defendant No.1. Ahmed Ali sold the suit land to Kala Miah Chowdhury on 29-10-36 for his son Nurul Islam Chowdhury who was a minor. After 9 years Kala Miah Chowdhury sold the suit land to the father of the plaintiff Aminur Rahman on 6-9-1945 by a registered kabala and Nurul Islam Chowdhury after attaining majority executed a deed of relinquishment on 18-2-1952 in favour of the plaintiffs' father. Defendants Nos. 1 to 3 had litigations and enmity. with the plaintiff and they obtained a collusive kabala in favour of defendant No.1 from the said Nurul Islam Chowdhury, defendant No. 4 on 25-4-1967 and threatened the possession of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 105 of 1967 for permanent injunction against the defendants. That suit, however, was dismissed and the appeal preferred against the order of dismissal was also dismissed. The plaintiffs contended that being encouraged by the order of dismissal of the suit and the appeal the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land on 22-9-1968 and hence the suit had been filed on 10-5-1976 for confirmation of title and recovery of khas possession. 

 5. The appellate Court below considered that this approach was wrong inasmuch as the O.S.No.105 of 1967 was a suit for simply permanent injunction; admittedly there was no final adjudication regarding the title and recovery of khas possession.
